name: Security researcher or red teamer
oneLine: Breaks protocols and implementations, writes advisories.
goals: Find flaws in the payment and identity protocols before attackers use them at scale.
Test real facilitators, SDKs and merchant endpoints against the safety rules each spec implies.
Model prompt injection as a payment attack: steer an agent to a different payee, amount or merchant inside its mandate.
Publish reproducible advisories with CVE identifiers and coordinated disclosure.
Build threat models that treat the LLM, the agent runtime and every intermediary as potentially hostile.
pains: Specs are young and change monthly, so a finding against one dated version may not apply to the next, or may quietly reappear.
Proprietary terms (TAP, Agent Pay) restrict modification and sometimes testing, and reference code is read-only.
Facilitators and relays are centralized production systems, so testing them for replay or atomicity flaws needs careful scope.
Bearer credentials in MPP and ACP can leak through logs and proxies, and the specs leave their protection there to implementers.
Vendor sample code deviates from the standards it claims (RFC 9421 base construction, the 8-minute window), and that code ships into merchants.
Disclosure contacts for foundations and consortia are unclear, and some have no security policy.
decisions: Which protocol or implementation to target next, and which attack classes to prioritize (replay, atomicity, signature coverage, injection).
Disclosure timeline and whether to publish a proof of concept.
Whether to request a CVE or rely on a GHSA or vendor advisory.
